title: Solution Advocacy Lab: Partner Sell‑Through Strategy & Evidence Pack
author: Samira Khan
body:
Overview:

This playbook (the Solution Advocacy Lab) is designed to equip partner account teams, systems integrators, and channel engineers with a single, evidence-driven kit for sell‑through of Redwood Inference to platform and ISV customers. It focuses on three objectives: (1) concise positioning for technical and economic decision makers, (2) compact competitive rebuttals and battlecards, and (3) templated collateral (pitch outline, ROI scenarios, security FAQ) that teams can reuse and localize.

TL;DR:
- Position Redwood as the production‑grade inference layer that reduces per‑token cost while preserving output quality and providing deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Use the "workload-first" economic story: show live throughput/lower latency and 20–60% token cost improvement via batching + KV caching + quantization recommendations.
- Lead with an ROI scenario (pilot → 6‑month run rate) and attach a short security evidence pack for CISO review.

1) Key positioning statements (single‑sentence hooks):
- For platform teams who need predictable inference economics and enterprise controls, Redwood delivers a unified runtime and toolset to run, monitor, and optimize LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Unlike single‑model APIs, Redwood optimizes at the serving layer—intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and model routing—so customers get consistent latency, lower unit cost, and safe fallbacks.

2) Audience-specific messages (3 lines each):
- CTO / Platform Engineering: "Run inference at scale with predictable latency and per‑token economics; pin model versions, use canary rollouts, and keep observability across routes and models."
- Head of ML / Lead ML Engineer: "Ship quality with model versioning, rollout control, and integrated evals to guard against degradations during quantization or model swaps."
- CISO / Security: "Deploy in VPC or air‑gapped on‑prem mode, integrate with KMS/HSM, and get audit logs for every request—no vendor data retention by default in Private mode."
- Product Manager / Growth PM: "Prototype on hosted API, then switch to Dedicated for predictable cost when the feature scales—no code changes required."

3) Competitive brief (summary + recommended rebuttals):
- Primary competitor themes we face: (A) simple model-access APIs (fast to adopt, weaker operational SLOs); (B) cloud-managed endpoints tied to a cloud vendor (harder multi‑cloud or private deployment); (C) self‑hosted inference stacks (control but high ops burden).
- Rebuttals and evidence points:
  - Against model-access APIs: emphasize SLA, routing/fallback, and cost controls (token-level dashboards, batching recommendations). Provide 95th/99th p50 latency comparisons for a 2048 token sequence.
  - Against cloud provider endpoints: emphasize deployment parity (same API across hosted/dedicated/private), lower middle-mile latency via regional routing, and enterprise-grade rollout mechanics.
  - Against self‑hosted vendors: cite time‑to‑value and maintenance burden; show migration path from PoC to Dedicated to Private with effort estimates (pilot: 2–4 weeks; Dedicated baseline: 6–10 weeks; Private: 8–16 weeks depending on networking).

4) Battlecard (one‑page script for SEs):
- Lead: "Are you optimizing inference costs or just buying model access?"
- Pain anchors: token overages, unpredictable tail latency, regressions after quantization, vendor lock‑in.
- Product levers to highlight: batching policies, KV/prefix cache, quantization profiles (4‑bit/8‑bit guidance), canary rollouts, model routing policies, tracing hooks in Console.
- Quick win demo suggestions (5–10 minutes): low-latency text generation with streaming, embedding + reranking flow, live dashboard showing token cost drop after enabling caching.

5) Pricing guidance (scenarios and anchoring language):
- Guiding principle: price to reflect three levers—model class (decoder/encoder/decoder‑only), deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), and unit economics improvements (batching + cache).
- Example scenarios (for sales conversations):
  - PoC (Developer Pilot): hosted API, up to 100k tokens / month, free credits or deeply discounted rates to prove latency and functional fit.
  - Growth Pilot: Dedicated burst pool estimate: commit to $Xk/month (example anchor $15k) for predictable throughput and 20–30% discounted unit rate vs hosted list.
  - Enterprise Production: Private/VPC with platform fee + committed GPU hours—price as custom quote with typical contract size $250k–$2M ARR depending on scale and support.
- How to use the ROI artifact: plug in customer throughput, average tokens per request, desired latency SLO; we produce a 6‑month run‑rate delta vs third‑party API. (See ROI snippet below.)

ROI calculator snippet (CLI example for SEs):

echo "{\"monthly_requests\":100000,\"avg_tokens\":120,\"hosted_rate_per_1k_tokens\":0.06,\"redwood_deltas\":{\"batching_efficiency\":0.4,\"cache_hit_rate\":0.15}}" > input.json
python tools/roi_estimator.py --input input.json

(Attach the shared spreadsheet template from the Partner Kit when engaging.)

6) Pitch deck outline (10 slides, minimal copy):
- Title: One‑liner + customer logo slide
- Problem: engineering and economic pain (latency, unit cost, regressions)
- How we solve it: serving runtime + tooling + unified deployment modes
- Demo screenshots: Console dashboards, cost breakdown, traces
- ROI: 6‑month scenario + sensitivity analysis
- Security & compliance: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO plan
- Migration path: PoC → Dedicated → Private (timeline & owners)
- Case study snapshot: 3 metrics (latency improvement, cost delta, time‑to‑production)
- Commercial ask: pilot commitment and success criteria
- Appendix: SLOs, technical architecture, contact info

7) Reusable email templates (short):
- Intro to technical contact:
  Subject: Quick run at inference latency & cost for [Customer]
  Body: Hi [Name], we can show a 2x latency improvement and ~30% token cost reduction for [workload]. Can we run a 2‑week pilot using your dev dataset?

- CISO intro (short):
  Subject: Security evidence & deployment options for Redwood Inference
  Body: Hi [Name], Redwood supports VPC/private deployments, KMS integration, and per‑request audit logs. I can share our evidence pack and SOC2 roadmap.

8) Case study (field narrative for prospects):
- Customer: Acme Logistics (global 3PL, anonymized)
- Challenge: Chat and summarization workloads spiking with peak onboarding flows—excessive token spend and 99th p latency incidents impacting customer SLA.
- Intervention: 6‑week pilot on Dedicated with batching policy + prefix caching and a 4‑bit quantization profile for a reranking model.
- Results: average latency down 38%, 6‑month projected token cost reduction 42%, time to production 7 weeks, no observable quality regression in top‑k precision.
- Quote (paraphrased): "Redwood let us move from experiment to production in weeks, with measurable savings and predictable behavior."

9) Security FAQ (short list for prospect packet):
- Q: Where is customer data stored for hosted deployments?
  A: Hosted keeps ephemeral request logs for debugging and billing; customers can opt out. Private and Dedicated modes keep data in customer VPCs or on‑prem.
- Q: How do you manage keys and encryption?
  A: Integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via KMIP; data encrypted at rest (AES‑256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Q: Do you retain model outputs or customer inputs?
  A: By default, Redwood retains minimal metadata for billing/traceability; retention policies are configurable and can be disabled for Private mode.
- Q: Compliance artifacts available?
  A: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 roadmap, penetration test summaries on request, and customer audit support for Private deployments.
- Q: Can we run air‑gapped?
  A: Yes—on‑prem air‑gapped packaging is supported with professional services engagement.

10) Execution playbook for a partner SE (step‑by‑step):
1. Qualification (0–1 days): confirm workload type, average tokens, latency SLO, network constraints, security buyer.
2. Offer pilot (1–2 days): propose 2‑week hosted or Dedicated pilot with clear success metrics (latency p95 target, cost delta target, eval prompt set).
3. Run pilot (2 weeks): deliver scripts for workload replay, preconfigured batching + cache profile, and a dashboard.
4. Analyze (2–3 days): produce short report with cost/latency/quality tradeoffs and recommended next steps.
5. Convert (2–6 weeks): propose Dedicated or Private deployment and provide migration timeline and ownership matrix.

11) Owner and escalation matrix: (table style)
- Partner SE: Samira Khan — pilot design and field execution
- Solution Architect: Ethan Blake — technical integration and trials
- Security SME: Priya Menon — evidence and CISO brief
- Account Exec: Diego Alvarez — commercial negotiation
- Escalation path: SE → SA → Sales Engineering Lead → Head of GTM

12) Appendix: supporting assets to attach in partner kit (checklist):
- ROI spreadsheet (editable)
- Short pitch deck (10 slides)
- Battlecard PDF and one‑pager
- Technical runbook for pilots (CLI scripts, dataset replay)
- Security evidence pack (SOC2 summary, pen test, KMS integration docs)

Contact / Next steps:
- Use this playbook as the master template. Localize messages and attach customer screenshots where possible. For help running a live ROI with a prospect, contact Samira Khan (se@redwood.ai).
